fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Second Wave of Volunteers", "body": "Kerri says the idea arrived as the prompt for her 2019 book, along with a nudge toward Dolores Cannon's talk on three waves of volunteers who have been arriving since the 1960s. In her telling, the second wave exists to embody higher frequencies, and that first required fully embracing humanity, which meant forgetting who they are. She dates the dawning awareness to around 2010 and 2011, and says anyone sensing there is more to the story than a name and a family belongs to the movement."}, {"title": "Fate, Destiny and Being Cherished", "body": "Chance asks about the Book of Fate and the Book of Destiny, and Kerri describes the first as the storyline handed to us at birth, one she says each soul chose in a time of great change. The second, she says, can be opened only by the soul, and doing so does not mean killing the personality. Instead the personality discovers how cherished it is, even in the parts it finds gritty, while she makes room for real pain along the way."}, {"title": "Motherhood and the Mother Wound", "body": "Chance reads Dolores Cannon's observation that many first and second wavers avoid having children, then asks whether cultural messaging aimed at young women might be an effort to reduce the number of third wave souls arriving. Kerri answers that those who chose children signed up to heal the mother wound, a specialized task she explores in her newer book, and she honors those who chose another role, such as holding space. She envisions motherhood grounded in natural authority rather than control."}, {"title": "How White Eagle Entered Her Story", "body": "Kerri describes White Eagle as an ascended master whose method is rainbow light and whose path is the red road of indigenous teaching, aimed at lifting consciousness past the reptilian and limbic brains toward the frontal cortex and an open heart. She traces the meeting to a drum journey in which, eyes closed, she says she saw a chief in a white feathered headdress, later matched to a photograph she had never seen. Chance adds his own view that perception is routed through one aperture, the optic thalamus."}, {"title": "Emergency, Witnessing and Thinking for Yourself", "body": "Chance wonders how to take the scariness out of the word emergency and offers the pun that it is literally emergent, which Kerri embraces, describing heavy fear-based energy that rises to be felt and witnessed before it can leave and contrasting it with spiritual bypass, floating out of the body instead of embodying. She calls the body the vehicle of spirituality, and Chance agrees that purifying the temple prevents distortion. Her Skills Not Pills message urges people to think, research and feel for themselves, since she says no one size fits all answer remains, and Chance adds that this age asks us to know rather than believe."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Kerri Hummingbird is the author of several books, and host of her own podcast: Soul Nectar. Join us for a discussion about Kerri's 2019 book, The Second Wave: Transcending The Human Drama, a book about getting past the amnesiac state of life on Earth, and remembering the gifts your soul always intended to bring to this life.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: We also talk about her partner of sorts on this project, White Eagle; he's a Native ancestor who connects with Kerri in the astral to give guidance. Other topics include Kerri's "Skills Not Pills" Movement, communicating with our own ancestors, spiritual emergencies, and what it feels like to open our third eye apertures to a higher vibration of reality.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Butterfly Cocoon for Humanity", "body": "Answering Chance's question about stay at home orders, Kerri argues the conversation should be lifted away from ideas of demonic control and toward an evolutionary process, with the butterfly as its emissary. In her telling, the creature digests itself into soup, imaginal cells build something new at a higher vibration, and helping it out of the cocoon would kill it. Chance links imaginal cells to the imaginal realm where ancestors are met, and Kerri says those who have emerged are weaving a planetary grid of conversations."}, {"title": "Separation as a Chosen Experiment", "body": "Chance reads a passage from Kerri's book comparing Earth to an imbalanced gut biome, with entities that farm human emotional energy, and asks how to take ownership instead of playing the victim. Kerri offers a cookie craving parasite analogy, calls the entities cleaners, and says souls collectively agreed to experience separation, like a family Monopoly game some now want to leave. She names them coyote teachers whose triggers reveal our shadows, while Chance suggests they are natural rather than morally evil."}, {"title": "Toxic People as Mirrors", "body": "Chance suggests that empaths who flee so-called toxic people may be overlooking their power to transmute, and says entities feed on what they absorb, though he insists on healthy boundaries and on asking inwardly whether to stay or bow out. Kerri offers a velcro metaphor: what sticks is a matching piece inside you, and reclaiming it lets the other person slide off your field. Compassion follows, she says, as recognition of sovereignty rather than pity, and Chance hears in that a reclaimed meaning of witness."}, {"title": "Stones, Mesas and Crystal Grids", "body": "Asked about native ways with crystals, Kerri explains her Andean shamanic training, where medicine stones live inside a mesa bundle she carries daily, chosen by feeling drawn to them and then checked against what she is working on. She also uses altars, meditation with a stone on the third eye, and crystal grids that set ground rules for a space. Chance shares his selenite practice and a story he heard of someone who gridded Chicago with raw selenite."}, {"title": "Firewalking and the Stories of the Mind", "body": "Kerri says firewalking dismantles the childhood rule that fire is bad, like pulling a low block from a Jenga tower, and that attending a workshop lets you watch the mind invent catastrophes. She recalls her first walk feeling like cold wet grass, now leads walks with singing rather than shouting, and reads a small blister as a pointer to a blocked meridian, a view she offers from her own experience and pairs with advice to walk only with trained leaders. Chance replies with the idea of being permeable, not vulnerable."}]
